# **Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – no standardised first-touch-to-first-class journey; risk of inconsistent induction, safety gaps, goal capture
- **Member Checkins** – no cadence or script for retention touchpoints; early churn likely going undetected
- **Cancellation & Churn** – no win-back process or exit interview; losing data on why members leave
- **Member Pause** – no criteria, approval process, or re-engagement trigger; pauses likely becoming silent cancellations
- **Referral Programme** – no mechanics, incentives, or tracking; leaving organic word-of-mouth unstructured
- **Member data privacy & GDPR** – no documented handling of personal/payment/health data; compliance and liability risk
- **Weekly Key Coach Tasks** – no standardised weekly coaching priorities; coaching inconsistency, performance variance
- **Coaching Development Roadmap** – no clear progression, upskilling, or assessment framework; retention and quality ceiling
- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – no mechanism to audit class delivery, safety, energy; quality drift undetected
- **Troubleshooting Guide** – no playbook for common member complaints (injury concerns, billing, class fit, equipment); ad-hoc responses

# Service Menu Build — Execution Plan for Grace

• **Audit revenue reality FIRST** — Before writing anything, pull last 3 months of actual transactions. What are people *actually* buying? Group by service type (classes, PT, challenges, merchandise). Your menu should reflect what's working, not what you think should work. Surprises will guide pricing decisions.

• **Split into two separate documents immediately** — Staff version lists margins, upsells, and decision trees ("If member asks X, recommend Y"). Member version is clean, benefit-focused, price-only. They're not the same document. Staff need to sell; members need clarity.

• **Price anchor around your most popular service** — If group classes are your volume driver, price that as your "normal." Price everything else relative to it (PT should be 3-4x a class, challenges 1.5x). Don't calculate in a vacuum. Members compare internally.

• **Include the invisible stuff** — Community access, app features, booking priority, or coach access (whatever you actually offer). Members don't know what they're getting. Write it down. Then you can charge for it or use it as upgrade bait.

• **Test with 5 coaches + 5 members this week** — Share drafts, watch where they hesitate or ask questions. Those friction points are pricing or clarity problems. One round of feedback, then lock it down and publish.
